h1: Chala Number 6 — Boutique Luxury in the Old City, Just a Few Steps from Wat Chedi Luang
intro: Picture this: a few steps out the hotel door and you're standing in front of the ancient chedi at Wat Chedi Luang, with the Sunday Walking Street waiting around the corner come evening — yet step back into your room and it's as quiet as a resort outside town. Chala Number 6 is a 5-star boutique hotel that many people choose because it offers both an old-city location and a private, restful feel in one place · opened in 2017, renovated in 2023 · large suites decorated in bright Thai tones, from around THB 3,500/night · scored 9.3 from over 710 reviews

body.html: If there's one hotel that nails the idea of "staying in the old city without giving up the quiet," people who visit Chiang Mai often tend to name Chala Number 6 first · the hotel sits on Prapokklao Road in the Si Phum–Phra Sing area, right in the heart of Chiang Mai's moated old city · the standout everyone agrees on is a location that's practically next to Wat Chedi Luang — walk out the door and in under five minutes you'll find the old temple, coffee shops, and the walking street, yet step back inside the hotel grounds and the traffic and tourist noise fade away surprisingly fast · the hotel has been open since 2017 and recently went through a major renovation in 2023, so the rooms and facilities still look fresh and well kept

Who it suits — from real reviews, Chala Number 6 works well for couples wanting a romantic feel in the middle of town, working travelers who want an easy place to relax after a full day of sightseeing, and families looking for large rooms in a spot where you can get around on foot without relying on a car · the hotel has Family Rooms in several sizes, while the overall atmosphere stays fairly quiet and rest-focused, so it suits people who want calm over a poolside party · if you're a backpacker chasing the absolute cheapest rate, this may not be your first pick, but if you want a luxury feel on a budget that's still reasonable compared to the big 5-star brands, this is where many people say it's better value than expected

Location and getting around — the address is 6/6 Prapokklao Road, Phra Sing subdistrict, inside the old moated city · Wat Phan Tao is only about 120 meters away and Wat Chedi Luang about 170 meters, both within a three-minute walk · the Sunday Walking Street runs right through this area, so on Sunday evenings you can practically step out the hotel door and walk straight into the market · Tha Phae Gate is about 500 meters away, an easy 8–10 min walk, while Nimmanhaemin Road is about 10–15 min away by car · Chiang Mai International Airport (CNX) is about 5 km away, around a 12–15 min drive · the upside of this location is that you can walk to nearly all the temples and restaurants in the old city without calling a car, but one thing to note is that the lane in front of the hotel is fairly narrow, so if you're driving yourself you should ask about parking in advance, even though the hotel does offer free parking

Rooms and decor — this is where Chala Number 6 sets itself apart from the usual boutique · the hotel has around 82 rooms, each fairly spacious; even the entry-level Junior Suite has about 55 sqm or more, while the family rooms and Grand Suite stretch to 76–78 sqm · the decor uses bold, bright contemporary Thai tones, mixing woven fabrics, Lanna patterns, and wooden furniture with the comfort of a modern hotel · many rooms have tall four-poster beds and large windows, and some open a back door directly onto the garden or central courtyard · bathrooms are finished in marble with rain showers, and some rooms have smart toilets and a capsule coffee machine · real reviews praise how clean the rooms are and how comfortable the beds, though some note that the wardrobe in certain suite types is on the small side, and rooms without a balcony have fairly small windows that let in less natural light

"Waking up, opening the door, and sitting by the pool with a single coffee and the sound of birds in the garden — hard to believe that a few more steps out the door is Wat Chedi Luang in the middle of town."

Facilities, pool, and spa — the heart of the hotel is the outdoor pool set in the middle of the garden, ringed by palm trees and green foliage · many real reviews say the pool is especially pretty at sunset, with a whirlpool corner to soak and relax in, and water deep enough for an actual swim, not just a dip · there's a small bar by the pool for ordering drinks · on top of that there's a free fitness room and Waya Spa, offering massages and facials with local herbs · what many guests love most is the free afternoon tea at the wooden rice barn in the garden, with snacks, fruit, and at certain times a short sample massage of around 10 min to try for free · little details like these are what make many guests feel they're getting more care than they paid for

Food and bar — the hotel's main restaurant is No.6 Restaurant, serving both Asian and Western dishes · breakfast is a buffet included in several room packages, served in the morning from around 6:30–10:30 AM, with international options as well as local Thai food, Thai sweets, drinks, and a made-to-order egg station · real reviews say breakfast tastes good and the ingredients are fresh, even if the choices aren't as many as at a big chain hotel, which makes sense for a place this size · a common note is that the breakfast room is fairly small, so during busy times you may have to wait for a table · for other meals, the old-city location is an advantage, because a few steps out and you'll find northern restaurants, coffee shops, and street food all around Wat Chedi Luang to choose from

What's worth walking to nearby — the advantage of the old-city location is that everything is within walking distance · start with Wat Chedi Luang and its huge centuries-old chedi, open from morning to evening, beautifully lit at night · not far on is Wat Phan Tao, a quiet old teak-wood viharn, and Wat Chiang Man, the city's first temple · on Sunday evenings the walking street starts setting up around four in the afternoon, selling crafts, food, and souvenirs all along Ratchadamnoen Road · around the hotel you'll also find stylish cafes, khao soi spots, nam ngiao rice-noodle shops, and traditional northern restaurants to try all week · many real reviews say this location is the main reason they chose to stay here, because the moment you leave your room you can start exploring without wasting time on a ride into town

Service — the thing that consistently earns the most praise in reviews is the staff · many guests describe the staff as smiling, friendly, and attentive to little details, like decorating the room for special occasions, welcome desserts, or bath salts to use with the whirlpool · some reviews mention being welcomed so warmly that they felt like an important guest rather than just a passing customer · the front desk is open 24 hours and can help arrange transfers or tours · overall, the service is one of the main reasons the hotel's combined score reaches as high as 9.3

Real reviews — the good and the not-so-good · on the praise side, the recurring points are a location within easy walking distance of the temples and the walking street, rooms that are large and very clean, a pretty pool especially in the evening, service that's better than the price suggests, and the free afternoon tea as a lovely surprise · on the notes-to-know-before-booking side, there's the soundproofing between rooms that some feel isn't quite good enough, so you may hear noise from the next room or the hallway, rooms without a balcony having small windows and little light, limited storage space in some rooms, and a fairly small breakfast room · no reviews say it's bad enough to be disappointing — most are minor notes that don't dent overall satisfaction

What sets Chala Number 6 apart from the usual boutique — Chiang Mai's old city has hundreds of Lanna-style hotels and guesthouses, but what gets this one talked about is the way it blends being a "city hotel" with the feel of a "relaxing resort" in one space · many people expect a hotel in the middle of the moat to be cramped with no greenery, but once inside you find a garden, a pool, and a wooden rice barn that make it feel like you've slipped away from the bustle of the street out front · another thing regulars like to mention is the consistency — no matter when you stay, you get the same level of cleanliness, service, and atmosphere, which is rare for a small hotel · the major 2023 renovation also keeps the rooms and common areas looking fresh rather than worn with age · all of this is why the review scores keep holding above 9

Price and value comparison — entry-level room rates usually run around THB 3,500–THB 5,000 per night in normal periods, and can climb in high season or during festivals, with the larger suites and Grand Suite running noticeably higher · compared with the big 5-star brands in Chiang Mai at similar prices but usually located outside the moat, Chala Number 6 has the edge on its old-city location and rooms larger than average · add in the free afternoon tea, the good breakfast, and the well-reviewed service, and many people conclude this is one of the boutiques that gives the most reasonable luxury-on-a-budget feel in the old-city area · we'd always recommend comparing prices across platforms before booking, since Agoda, Booking, and Trip.com often have different promotions and breakfast-inclusive packages

Things to know before booking — if you're sensitive to noise, we'd suggest asking for a room set deeper in from the main hallway or one that opens onto the garden, to avoid disturbances · if you want natural light and a private sitting area, specify a room with a balcony or a garden door when you book, since some room types have small windows · in high season (November–February) and during the Yi Peng/Loy Krathong festivals, rooms fill up fast and prices rise high, so book several weeks ahead · because the lane in front of the hotel is narrow, if you're driving yourself, ask the hotel about the access route and parking first · and don't forget to ask about the timing of the free afternoon tea at check-in so you don't miss it

Summary — Chala Number 6 is a boutique hotel that suits people who want to stay in Chiang Mai's old city with everything within walking distance, while still getting the quiet and the luxury feel back in their room · its strengths are a location practically next to Wat Chedi Luang and the walking street, large clean rooms, a pretty pool, warm service, and little touches like the free afternoon tea that make you feel looked after · the limitations to accept are the imperfect soundproofing, the small breakfast room, and some room types with little light · if you're looking for a hotel that feels 5-star on an attainable budget, right in the old city, and you're not bothered by the minor notes above, this is a choice that most reviewers come back to recommend with confidence

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Chala Number 6 Chiang Mai

faq.q: Where is Chala Number 6 in Chiang Mai, and what's nearby?
faq.a: Chala Number 6 is located at 6/6 Prapokklao Road, in the Phra Sing–Si Phum area, in the heart of the old moated city · under a 3 min walk to Wat Chedi Luang and Wat Phan Tao · the Sunday Walking Street is around the corner · Tha Phae Gate is about an 8–10 min walk · Chiang Mai Airport is about a 12–15 min drive

faq.q: What's the starting price at Chala Number 6, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around THB 3,500/night for a Junior Suite of about 55 sqm · there are Superior/Deluxe Family Rooms and the Chala Grand Suite at 76–78 sqm · prices depend on the dates and package, so always compare across platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Chala Number 6 best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, working travelers who want an easy place to relax, and families wanting a large room in the old city · the atmosphere is quiet and rest-focused, and you can walk to the temples and the walking street without relying on a car · ideal for people who want a 5-star feel on an attainable budget

faq.q: Does Chala Number 6 really have free afternoon tea?
faq.a: Yes · real reviews confirm there is free afternoon tea at the wooden rice barn in the garden, with snacks, fruit, and at certain times a short sample massage of around 10 min to try · we'd recommend asking about the serving time at check-in so you don't miss it

faq.q: What are the downsides of Chala Number 6 to know before booking?
faq.a: The common notes are that the soundproofing between rooms isn't quite good enough, so you may hear the next room · rooms without a balcony have small windows and little light · the breakfast room is fairly small · we'd suggest asking for a garden-facing room to avoid noise and get better light

faq.q: Where can you book Chala Number 6, and how far ahead should you book?
faq.a: You can book through Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com, which often have different promotions and breakfast-inclusive packages, so always compare prices before booking · in high season (Nov–Feb) and during the Yi Peng/Loy Krathong festivals, book several weeks ahead since rooms fill up fast and prices rise high
